prologue.text: A solicitor travels east on business, carrying a letter from a count he has never met.

scenes.name: The Golden Krone Inn
scenes.setting: Bistritz, on the eve of St. George’s Day. The innkeeper and his wife receive Jonathan with uneasy courtesy while a coach waits to carry him east.
scenes.openingNarration: The inn is warm, but the welcome is not. A letter from Count Dracula promises a carriage at the Borgo Pass; the old woman who brought it looks as though she would rather bar the door than see you leave.

resolution.narration: The old woman places the crucifix around your neck and whispers a blessing. You cannot explain her fear, but you carry the protection with you.
The innkeeper refuses the Count’s name and crosses himself. His silence tells you more than an answer would: the road east is feared here.
You thank them and leave before the coach can wait any longer. The innkeeper watches you go with the expression of a man witnessing a mistake.

actions.label: Board the coach into the darkness
actions.shortLabel: Board the coach into the darkness

resolution.narration: The coach pulls away from Bistritz. The last lights of the Golden Krone vanish behind you as the road climbs toward the Borgo Pass.

scenes.name: The Borgo Pass
scenes.setting: The coach leaves the known road behind. Passengers cross themselves as darkness gathers among the mountains.
scenes.openingNarration: At midnight, another carriage waits where no ordinary connection should be. Its driver’s face is hidden, the horses are unnaturally strong, and the passengers’ warnings have become prayers.

resolution.narration: You keep your eyes on the driver. He moves with impossible certainty through the mountain darkness, never needing the road to tell him where to turn.

actions.label: Hold the crucifix and endure the journey
actions.shortLabel: Hold the crucifix and endure the journey

resolution.narration: Your fingers close around the crucifix. The gesture does not make the mountains safer, but it gives your fear a shape and keeps you from surrendering to it.
The carriage stops before a vast, dark gate. Count Dracula is waiting alone to receive you.

scenes.name: The Castle Door
scenes.setting: A ruined castle above the pass. Dracula receives Jonathan with impeccable courtesy, though no servant appears and every door seems to belong to the host.
scenes.openingNarration: The Count welcomes you as a guest, but the castle offers no ordinary signs of life. The warmth of his manners and the desolation around him refuse to fit together.

resolution.narration: Dracula answers with old history and practiced courtesy. He offers knowledge freely enough to make your questions feel safe, while revealing nothing that would make the castle less strange.

actions.label: Study the castle doors and passages
actions.shortLabel: Study the castle doors and passages

resolution.narration: You count doors, windows, and stairways while pretending to admire the architecture. Several routes are locked; the castle has received you, but it has not agreed to let you leave.
You retire to the room prepared for you. The courtesy is complete; the lock on the outside of the door is not mentioned.

scenes.name: The Castle’s Unquiet Rooms
scenes.setting: Days pass in a castle where the doors are locked and the letters home are dictated. Jonathan’s professional records become the only honest witness left to him.
scenes.openingNarration: You are no longer a guest in any meaningful sense. Dracula controls the letters you send, the rooms you may enter, and the explanations you are expected to give. Somewhere beyond the locked doors, the castle contains dangers he does not want you to name.

actions.label: Write the truth in your journal
actions.shortLabel: Write the truth in your journal

resolution.narration: You record the locked doors, the impossible movements, and the women who came to your room. If the journal survives, it may become the evidence that your letters cannot be.

actions.label: Search the locked rooms for an exit
actions.shortLabel: Search the locked rooms for an exit

resolution.narration: You test the boundaries of the castle and find that your confinement is deliberate. The search gives you no escape, but it replaces vague dread with hard knowledge.

actions.label: Resist the women at the window
actions.shortLabel: Resist the women at the window

resolution.narration: The women approach with an appetite that is not human. Before they can reach you, Dracula’s command tears through the room and turns their hunger back upon itself.
